news.title: Somali referee dropped from 2026 FIFA World Cup after US entry denial
news.lede: Somalian referee Omar Artan, who was set to become the first Somali official to referee at a FIFA World Cup, has been dropped from the list of match officials after being denied entry to the United States. Artan, who was named the 2025 Confederation of African Football Men’s Referee of the Year, was barred from entering the country at Miami International Airport and is currently in Turkey. No reason has been publicly given by US immigration authorities. However, Somalia is among a number of countries included in a travel ban introduced by US President Donald Trump's administration.

news.title: Philippines women’s national football team secures qualification for 2027 FIFA Women’s World Cup
news.lede: News On AIR | March 19, 2026 1:13 PM. The Philippines women’s national football team have secured qualification for the 2027 FIFA Women’s World Cup after defeating the Uzbekistan women’s national football team 2-0 in a Women’s Asian Cup play-in match on the Gold Coast today. Angela Beard delivered a standout performance, opening the scoring early in the second half after earlier missed opportunities. She found the net in the 47th minute with a well-taken strike into the roof of the goal.

news.title: Oceania’s next generation ready for FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup qualifiers
news.lede: The next generation of women’s football talent in Oceania will take centre stage in Honiara over the next fortnight, with eight nations set to compete for the OFC U-16 Women’s Championship 2026 and a coveted pathway towards next year’s FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco. The tournament kicks off on Sunday September 6, with Cook Islands, Fiji, New Caledonia, New Zealand, Papua New Guinea, Samoa, Solomon Islands, Tonga and New Caledonia all eyeing continental success. news.title: “They Put Qatar’s Clothes on Him at the Moment of World Cup Victory”... Football Has Become Nothing More Than a Money Game [Book]
news.lede: The moment Lionel Messi had dreamed of all his life was quite different from what we had imagined. At the awards ceremony at Lusail Stadium in Qatar in 2022, Argentina’s sky-blue stripes were covered by a black outer garment just before he lifted the World Cup trophy. It was a traditional Arab robe called a bisht, which Qatar’s emir personally draped over Messi’s shoulders. The convention that the captain of the winning team should lift the trophy wearing only his national team jersey was broken.

news.title: Argentina's players embrace fans' new World Cup anthem
news.lede: As Argentina's World Cup 2026 gathers momentum, the Albiceleste faithful have found a new soundtrack. Four years after 'Muchachos' became inseparable from the team's triumphant run in Qatar, a fresh terrace anthem, 'La cuarta estrella' ('The Fourth Star'), has erupted in stadiums across North America and is now being sung by Lionel Messi and his teammates as their title defence continues. The song gathered momentum among Argentina supporters before being embraced by the squad following Tuesday's dramatic 3-2 comeback victory over Egypt in Atlanta, which sealed a place in the World Cup quarter-finals.
